newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Yanhua wins approval to offer A shares.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Yanhua wins approval to offer A shares.

text.p: Chinese chemical concern Beijing Yanhua High-tech Co Ltd said on Tuesday it has received the approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission to offer of 12 million A shares and to list the stock in Shenzhen.

The offer, which has been tentatively priced at 7.50 yuan per share, would be launched via the Shenzhen bourse's automated quotation system in the near future, a company spokesman told the China Securities Bulletin.
Beijing Securities has been named the chief underwriter for the offer, the spokesman said.
He said Yanhua had also obtained approval to list three million staff shares, issued at one yuan per share in 1993, along with the class A shares for domestic investors.
The official said that Yanhua aimed to use the proceeds from the A share offer to finance a petrochemical project.
Yanhua has forecast net earnings of 28.76 million yuan for 1996, against 18.66 million yuan last year, he said.
The company currently has total share capital of 45 million shares, including 36 million legal person shares and nine million staff shares.
